passage: I'm Aditi. During art period my friend Ishan nudged me and whispered, "Look at Yash's drawing, it's a potato. Say something, everyone's going to." A few girls were already giggling. I felt torn: I wanted Ishan to like me, but I also knew Yash was trying hard. My mouth stayed shut for a moment. Then I said, quiet but clear, "I don't want to," and took my pencil box to the front table. Ishan rolled his eyes. That evening he texted me: "sorry, that was mean of me". I had not expected that. Maybe saying no can make a friend think.

qa.q: What did Ishan say Yash's drawing looked like?
qa.a: He said it was a potato.

qa.q: Why did Aditi feel torn when Ishan nudged?
qa.a: Aditi wanted Ishan to like Aditi but also knew Yash was trying hard, so Aditi was pulled between fitting in and doing right.

qa.q: What could Aditi say if a friend pushes again to mock someone?
qa.a: Aditi can repeat "I don't want to" and walk away, as before, because real friends respect that.

qa.q: How might Ishan see Aditi's refusal afterwards?
qa.a: Ishan first rolled his eyes, but that evening he admitted it was mean, so the refusal seems to have made him think.

grounding: A child pressured by a friend to mock a classmate says no and walks away, and the friend reconsiders.

passage:
In the colony park in Hyderabad, Chinmay nudged Ritu. "Look at Deepu's cycle, it's older than my Dada. Say something funny. Everyone's waiting."
The other kids were already smirking.
Ritu felt torn. She wanted to be part of the group. But Deepu's face had gone tight.
She shook her head. "Nah. I don't want to." And she walked off towards the swings.
Chinmay called after her, "Spoilsport!" But no one said the joke.
Later, Chinmay came to the swings. "Were you angry at me?"
"Not angry. Just, it's not fun if it's mean."
Chinmay kicked the sand. "Yeah. Okay."

qa.q: What did Chinmay say about Deepu's cycle?
qa.a: That it was older than his Dada.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling when Chinmay nudged her?
qa.a: She felt torn between fitting in with the group and doing what was right.

qa.q: What did Ritu do that was wise?
qa.a: She said she didn't want to join in and walked off, which stopped the joke and later made Chinmay think.

qa.q: How might Chinmay feel after Ritu's answer at the swings?
qa.a: Chinmay may feel a bit embarrassed and thoughtful, realising the joke was mean.

grounding: A girl's friend nudges her to mock a classmate; she feels torn, says she does not want to and walks off, and her friend later reconsiders.

passage:
"Samir, look at Venu's haircut. Tell him he looks like a coconut."
"Why me?"
"Because you're funny. Everyone will laugh."
Samir looked at Venu, sitting alone by the window. "I don't want to, Joseph."
"Come on, don't be boring."
"It's not boring. I just don't want to make fun of him."
"You're no fun anymore."
Samir picked up his bag. "I'm going to the library."
At the door he heard Joseph say to someone else, "Forget it."
Later, Joseph found him in the library. "Was it that bad?"
"It would have been, for Venu."
Joseph was quiet. "Yeah. Maybe."

qa.q: What did Joseph want Samir to call Venu?
How did Samir feel when Joseph said he was no fun?
qa.a: He felt pressured and a bit stung, but stayed firm about not mocking Venu.

qa.q: What did Samir do that could make Joseph think?
qa.a: He said no calmly and walked away to the library, and when asked, he pointed out it would have hurt Venu.

qa.q: How might Joseph feel after talking to Samir in the library?
qa.a: Joseph seems uncertain and thoughtful, starting to see the joke from Venu's side.

grounding: A boy's friend nudges him to mock a classmate; he says he does not want to and walks off, and his friend starts to think about it.
